Step 1 is done, but only as tests: the compiler already enforced it before this brief, so I changed no checker code. Step 2 is not built; it needs your decision. The result is `partial`, committed locally as 95bfd5db.

**Step 1.** I added four test programs to `tests/compiler/tests/`. All four pass in a scratch project and `fmt --check` finds nothing to fix:
- **`a_view_into_a_field_changed_in_place_is_refused`**: a piece of a buffer put into a field that is later changed in place is refused with NK1106, and the help says to write `.clone()`.
- **`a_copy_into_a_field_changed_in_place_is_accepted`**: the same with `.clone()` runs.
- **`a_view_into_an_element_changed_in_place_is_refused`**: pieces pushed into a list whose element is changed afterwards are refused with NK1102 at the `push`, help `.clone()`.
- **`map_keys_from_a_buffer_stay_views`**: map keys, list elements and a struct's map field that are never changed stay views and are accepted.

Because the rule was already in place, the tests also pass on the old compiler, so there was no fails-before run. A test program's ledger is not recorded, so I checked the ledger by hand with `nikaia lower`: the struct's map field `counts` is listed as `tethered`, and the map keys and list elements show as `ref(text)`. With no Rust or `tools/*.nika` changed, I ran no build, `lower-std`, clippy or `it` tests.

**Step 2 conflicts with the specification.** The brief says to refuse b37's probe "with the existing escape error". But Part I 6.6 and NK2303 say a struct handed back whose views point into a local moves that local into the caller's anchor and is not refused. ADR-views-3 D5 and D8 name no such refusal either, and there is no escape error code to use. Things still open:
- b37's probe (a `ref L` field holding a view of a local, returned) still reaches rustc. The closest code for a refusal is NK2304 ("what the tether cannot lower"), but Part III lists only two cases for it. D4 also removes `ref` fields, so this spelling is going away anyway.
- The views-3 spelling also fails. A plain `own: L` field (`L` with a `String` field, so it is not copied) filled from `xs[0]` and returned reaches rustc with "Mismatched types".
- `go(l)` building `W { own: l }` and passing it to a function that only reads it gets NK2105 at the caller ("go keeps l"). D5's last paragraph calls that lending. Fixing it means a non-text field can be a view or own its value case by case. That is emitter work in `emit_*`, which is outside this lane.

The decision needed: refuse or anchor in the first case, and whether a lent non-text parameter counts as "a piece of a buffer" under D5. The report puts all of this, with the probes, under `Needs:`.

The test cache is 2.7G against the 2G limit, 7.7G free on disk. One new entry over 100 MB: `run-bundle/c1ccf85af4afe566` (211 MB).
